title: Financial mathematics
summary: Compound interest, depreciation and inflation, then loans and annuities solved with the GDC finance (TVM) solver.

keyterms.definition: Interest added to the balance so that later interest is earned on earlier interest: FV = PV(1 + r/(100k))ᵏⁿ.
The amount of money now, e.g. the amount invested or borrowed.
The value of an investment or loan balance at the end of a time period.
How often interest is added, e.g. yearly (k = 1), quarterly (k = 4) or monthly (k = 12).
The quoted yearly interest rate r%, divided between the compounding periods.
A fall in value over time; with a fixed annual percentage, the value is multiplied by (1 − r/100) each year.
A general rise in prices over time, reducing the real value (purchasing power) of money.
The GDC finance app that finds one unknown from N, I%, PV, PMT, FV, P/Y and C/Y.
A series of equal payments or deposits made at regular time intervals.
Repaying a loan with regular payments, each covering the interest due and reducing the principal.

questions.prompt: $5000 is invested at 4% per year compounded annually. Find its value after 6 years.
questions.explanation: FV = 5000 × 1.04⁶ = 6326.60. $6200 is the simple-interest value.

questions.text: In FV = PV(1 + r/(100k))ᵏⁿ, k is the number of compounding periods per ___.
questions.explanation: k = 12 for monthly compounding, 4 for quarterly, 1 for yearly.

questions.prompt: $3000 is invested at a nominal 6% per year compounded monthly. Find the value after 2 years.

questions.statement: For the same nominal annual rate, compounding monthly gives a larger final value than compounding annually.
questions.explanation: Interest added more often starts earning interest sooner.

questions.prompt: A car costing $28 000 depreciates by 15% per year. Find its value after 4 years.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 0.85 each year: 28 000 × 0.85⁴ = 14 616.18.

questions.statement: Depreciation of 15% per year means the value falls by the same dollar amount each year.
questions.explanation: A percentage depreciation falls by less each year in dollars because it is 15% of a shrinking value.

questions.prompt: An item costs $50 today. With 3% annual inflation, what will it cost in 10 years?
questions.explanation: 50 × 1.03¹⁰ = 67.20. Inflation compounds like interest.

questions.prompt: Match each TVM solver variable to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Entering the right values for each variable is the main skill with the finance app.

questions.text: A simple estimate of the real interest rate is the nominal rate minus the ___ rate.
questions.explanation: If savings grow 5% but prices rise 3%, purchasing power grows by about 2%.

questions.prompt: Order the value of $1000 after 1 year at 6% nominal, from smallest to largest, by compounding frequency.
questions.explanation: The values are 1060, 1060.90, 1061.36 and 1061.68: more frequent compounding gives slightly more.

questions.statement: In an amortized loan, each payment first pays the interest due and the rest reduces the principal.
questions.explanation: That is why the balance falls slowly at first and faster later.

questions.prompt: A $200 000 mortgage at 5% nominal compounded monthly is repaid monthly over 25 years. Find the monthly payment.
For the mortgage above (payments $1169.18), find the total interest paid.
questions.explanation: Total paid = 300 × 1169.18 ≈ 350 754, minus the 200 000 borrowed gives about 150 754.

questions.text: An ___ is a sequence of equal payments made at regular intervals.
questions.explanation: Savings plans and pensions paid out monthly are annuities.

questions.statement: Early in a long mortgage, most of each payment goes towards interest.
questions.explanation: Interest is charged on the large outstanding balance, so it takes most of the early payments.

questions.prompt: Sam saves $200 at the end of each month for 10 years at 3% nominal compounded monthly. Find the final value.
questions.explanation: TVM: N = 120, I% = 3, PV = 0, PMT = −200 gives FV ≈ 27 948.28; $24 000 is just the deposits.

questions.prompt: In the TVM solver, money you pay out (such as deposits or loan repayments) is entered as:
questions.explanation: The sign shows the direction of cash flow: money out is negative, money in is positive.

questions.prompt: Match each question to the TVM variable you solve for.

pairs.left: How much do I repay each month?
How long until savings reach my target?
What rate doubles money in 10 years?
How much must I invest today?

questions.explanation: Enter every known value, then solve for the unknown.

questions.prompt: Put one row of an amortization table in order.
items: Add the interest for the period

questions.text: A loan of $10 000 is charged 1% interest per month. The interest in the first month is $___.
